sourceInformation.source: Astro Battle / Space Invaders — Bally Astrocade; the supplied 1979 combined source wording is interpreted this way. The renamed manual bears a 1981 copyright.
sourceInformation.perspective: Fixed-screen overhead; screen-aligned horizontal cannon and upward fire.
sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript ES modules, Canvas2D and Web Audio; my-3D2dge handoff 0.89.1 at 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0 at 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869. Bun bundles development modules; the final HTML is self-contained.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded pixel silhouettes, hue-shifted ramps, three planetary outpost palettes, native procedural lighting and a crisp retro-modern cabinet presentation.
sourceInformation.animation: Native E.anim march poses, cannon recoil/readiness, armor break, bunker debris and repair highlights, saucer wobble, flagship emitters/core windows and planetary victory fireworks on the native fixed clock.
sourceInformation.audio: Original runtime oscillator instruments, generated noise, three sparse location themes, flagship music, result stingers, event effects and filtered gibberish voice bus. No audio files. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub host-authoritative shared-world co-op for 1–2 roster seats, reliable complete snapshots and acknowledged action heartbeats. Standalone supports solo and simultaneous local co-op.
sourceInformation.testing: One quiet command runs deterministic simulation and native headless drawing, ordinary-input complete STANDARD solo/co-op campaigns, Chromium integration, Firefox/WebKit smoke, emulated pads/phone/tablet, generated audio signal/mute probes, blocked/malformed storage and the pinned Hub harness with loss, latency, host departure and server hosting. Physical controller feel, human listening, real TV distance and real iOS behavior remain unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Examined archived manual transcription and PDF scan, contemporary Video Games October 1982 comparison, and archive-linked Nice and Games footage at 90/120 seconds plus sequential filmstrip. Exact source sound unknown: no human listening. Sources: ballyalley.com/cart_manuals/html_manuals/astro_battle.htm; ballyalley.com/astrocade_videos/cartridge_videos/cartridge_videos.html. Detailed evidence in research/RESEARCH.md.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux / Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS on WSL2; Node24.21.0; Python Playwright1.63.0; Chromium153.0.8010.12, Firefox155.0 and WebKit26.6.

testingFeedback: 25 unique issues were found and fixed through automated tests, native API/contract reviews and screenshot inspection. Repeated failures from the same cause are counted once; test-pilot timing and observation mistakes are excluded. The issue ledger is evidence/ISSUES.md.
2 critical defects: classic-script export syntax prevented boot, and a null native pad selector disabled solo controller discovery. Both are fixed and covered by regressions.

Ordinary-input STANDARD solo and co-op campaigns through all six formations and both flagship phases, using normal damage and resources. Native-controller and live Hub checks then verified that the same rules survive integration.
Menu screenshots captured before the entrance animation settled were least helpful. State assertions and settled screenshots gave clearer evidence.
engineFeedback: The readable native sprite, animation, hue-ramp, synthesized-audio and deterministic advance APIs give this small arcade game a coherent foundation.

I initially used incorrect native setting names and treated a null pad selector as automatic discovery. Reading the actual engine contracts and native regressions resolved these. The arcade helper also alternates turns, so simultaneous co-op uses the explicit shared world.
The serializable deterministic combat world: shared erodible bunker masks, lane-preserving repair, deployment accounting and host authority.
Keeping fixed combat bounds, local overlays and device ownership coherent across native rendering, menus and Hub lifecycle.
None. The full pinned engine remains intact; the application uses its supported custom-menu and autoPause:false options.
A documented serializable simulation/event adapter for small host-authoritative shared worlds would reduce integration work.
promptFeedback: The source-specific spatial decision, finite campaign and explicit acceptance paths made a clear game to build.
The two similar source names require an explicit interpretation; generic engine defaults also need reconciliation with the fixed-screen and co-op contracts.
Proving ordinary campaign completion while keeping standalone, local co-op, touch and Hub authority on the same rules.
Keep required behavior and deliverables separate from suggested file organization so acceptance is faster to audit.

aiHub.name: Orbit Invadettes
aiHub.tagline: Cut a lane. Catch the scrap. Keep your planet.
aiHub.description: Six marching alien formations threaten three planetary outposts. Cut firing lanes through your bunkers, catch salvage to repair them, and bring down an original hostile flagship alone or together.
aiHub.source: Astro Battle / Space Invaders — Bally Astrocade
aiHub.controls: Move: stick/D-pad, A/D/arrows or mouse; fire: R2/Cross, Space/left mouse; repair: L1/Square, Q/right mouse; pause/options: Options/Escape. Touch: relative drag, assisted fire, second-contact lane cutting and contextual repair.
